html:
San Agustín is a group of ancient burial sites in the hills of southern Colombia, near the source of the Magdalena River, with hundreds of carved stone statues made in the first centuries CE.

The statues, some over four metres tall, guard tombs and stand in mounds. They show gods, animals and fierce human figures with fangs, often holding tools or other beings. Little is known of the people who made them; they had no writing and had left by the time the Spanish came.

The site became a World Heritage Site in 1995 and is the best-known ancient monument of Colombia after Ciudad Perdida. Like the stone spheres of Costa Rica, it shows the chiefdoms that lay between the Maya world and the Andes.
sum: San Agustín is a group of ancient burial sites in the hills of southern Colombia, near the source of the Magdalena River, with hundreds of carved stone statues made in the first centuries CE.
